3. Radical Clearance and Demolition in the Flood Plain Area
This is the most drastic of the measures considered. While limited clearance and demolition on the flood plain is acceptable and practical, large scale or total clearance of the flood plain areas in Harrisburg would be as devasting to the economic, cultural and social fabric of the city as another flood several times greater than the flood of record. Not even taking into account the human aspect of such a program, the economics of such a proposal would be astronomical. Thus, pushing it far beyond the bounds of practicality. Total clearance of the flood plain would "gut" the heart of the City. It is most likely that public opinion could cause total rejection if such a proposal were to be seriously introduced as an alternate to the proposed project.
